content.body:
> **Tracking:** #6, the residual after the Phase 3 MVP translation service shipped (#17). Build the two adapters the MVP deliberately deferred: the Claude managed-agents (CMA) renderer and the mcp renderer.

## Problem

The translation service shipped as an MVP (#17): `scripts/translate.py` renders **skills** (native copy) and **agents** (opencode transform) and assembles the **Claude Code marketplace**, gated by `make ci`. Two capability cells in `primitives-core-translation-config.yaml` are configured but **not implemented** — they are recorded as skips, not rendered:

- **claude-agents (CMA)** — `scripts/translate.py:290-301` records every claude-agents target as `{"capability": "render", "reason": "claude-agents (CMA) adapter deferred (post-MVP)", "skipped": true}`. So `targets/claude-agents/` is empty (only `.gitkeep`) and the results lock carries 71 deferred skips. The adapters `cma_skill_upload` / `cma_agent_create` named at `primitives-core-translation-config.yaml:43,48` don't exist. The CMA contract is already pinned (CANON "Resolved — managed-agents (CMA) contract": `POST /v1/skills` multipart with `SKILL.md` at root; `POST /v1/agents` with `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams`).
- **mcp render** — `primitives-core-translation-config.yaml:50-53` configures `mcp_to_claude` / `mcp_to_opencode` / `mcp_to_cma`, but `primitives-core/mcp/` is **empty** (only `.gitkeep`), and the roster has **zero** `type: mcp` entries. There is nothing to render and nothing to test the renderer against — mcp render is blocked on a first mcp primitive existing.

This is the deferred half of #6; the MVP half (skills/agents/CC marketplace + drift guard) is done and closed via #17.

## Deliverables

- **A — CMA adapter** in `scripts/translate.py` (replaces the deferred-skip block at `:290-301`). Emit static, deterministic artifacts under `targets/claude-agents/`:
  - per skill targeting claude-agents: a build-sheet/manifest describing the `POST /v1/skills` multipart upload (the skill folder is uploaded as-is; `name`/`description` extracted from `SKILL.md`).
  - per agent: a `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams` payload JSON (`name`, `model`, `system` = agent body, `tools[]`, `skills[]` refs, `mcp_servers[]`).
  - record real (non-skip) results in `primitives-core-translation-results.json`; extend `make build-check`/CI to guard `targets/claude-agents/`.
- **B — mcp render adapter** (`mcp_to_claude` / `mcp_to_opencode` / `mcp_to_cma` in `scripts/translate.py`) — implement against the neutral `primitives-core/mcp/<name>.json` spec, **gated on a first mcp primitive existing** (see Dependencies). Until then, the cells stay `render`-configured but unexercised.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `targets/claude-agents/` is non-empty after `make build`: contains a CMA payload/manifest for every roster entry whose `targets` includes `claude-agents` (71 today).
- [ ] `primitives-core-translation-results.json` shows `claude-agents` entries with `"skipped": false` and a `destination` + `sha256` (grep for `"claude-agents (CMA) adapter deferred"` returns zero hits).
- [ ] Each generated agent payload is valid JSON and carries the required `BetaManagedAgentsCreateAgentParams` fields `name` + `model` (verifiable: `python3 -c` loads each and asserts the keys).
- [ ] Build is deterministic — `make build` twice produces byte-identical `targets/claude-agents/` + lock (the existing run-twice check extended to the new target).
- [ ] `make ci` (drift guard) green: `translate.py --check` covers `targets/claude-agents/`.
- [ ] **B (mcp):** when a `type: mcp` primitive is added to the roster, `make build` renders it to each target without a code change to the adapters; `make ci` stays green. (If no mcp primitive is added in this issue, B is split to a follow-up — see Out of scope.)

## Dependencies & gates

- **Blocks on:** Deliverable B blocks on a first `type: mcp` primitive existing in `primitives-core/mcp/` + the roster — there is none today, so B cannot be exercised or tested until one lands. A is unblocked (real inputs exist).
- **Gates that fire:** `make ci` (the roster + targets drift guards) — always; **targets drift guard** (`make build-check`, fix with `make build`) — this changes generated `targets/` output, so the lock must be regenerated in the same PR; `yamllint`/`actionlint` if the config or CI workflow changes.
- **Gates that do NOT fire:** roster↔disk (`make check`) only matters if primitives change — A/B add no primitives (B's mcp primitive, if added, would trigger it); no DB / infra / API-codegen gates in this repo.
- **Contract to keep in sync:** the CMA contract in CANON "Resolved — managed-agents (CMA) contract" — if the adapter deviates from the pinned `POST /v1/skills` / `POST /v1/agents` shapes, amend that note in the same change.

## Out of scope

- **Live API calls / uploading** to the managed-agents API — the adapter emits **static payloads/build-sheets** only; actually POSTing them is a deploy-time concern (dotfiles-bootstrap), not the translation build.
- Model-id mapping for CMA agent payloads beyond carrying the agent's stated tier (the opencode transform already omits model; same simplification applies unless a mapping is decided).
- If no mcp primitive is created here, **Deliverable B becomes a tracked follow-up** ("render the first mcp primitive") rather than blocking A from closing #6's CMA half.

> **Origin:** surfaced by the #22 test suite. `translate.py` reads files with `open(...).read()` and never closes them; the new tests raise `ResourceWarning`s (currently silenced in the runner via `-W ignore::ResourceWarning`).

## Problem

`scripts/translate.py` opens files without closing them in several hot paths -- e.g. the parsers (`:56`, `:109`), `sha256_path` (`:185`), `skill_display_title` (`:226`), and others use `open(path).read()` / `for raw in open(path)`. Under the unit tests this surfaces as `ResourceWarning: unclosed file`, which `make test` currently hides with `-W ignore::ResourceWarning`. The leak is benign in the short-lived CLI but is a latent correctness/style issue and forces the test runner to suppress a whole warning class.

## Deliverables

- A -- wrap every read in `translate.py` in a `with` block (or a small `read_text(path)` / `read_bytes(path)` helper) so no handle leaks.
- B -- drop the `-W ignore::ResourceWarning` suppression from the `make test` target once the leaks are gone.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `python3 -W error::ResourceWarning -m unittest discover -s tests -t .` passes with **zero** `ResourceWarning` (warnings-as-errors).
- [ ] `make test` no longer needs `-W ignore::ResourceWarning`.
- [ ] `make ci` stays green and `targets/` is byte-identical (pure refactor, no output change).

## Dependencies & gates

- `make ci` aggregate: FIRES -- the targets drift guard must stay green (no rendered-output change).
- Roster / naming gates: do NOT fire (no primitive or plugin touched).

## Out of scope

- Any behavior or output change in the translation service (this is a pure resource-handling refactor).
- Broader refactors of `translate.py` beyond closing file handles.

> **Tracking:** #40, from the dotfiles-agents-cowork desk (standards-curation thread; follows
> the project-workflow conformance pass, `_meta/plans/project-workflow-conformance.md`). Extend
> the repo meta-structure standard so `docs/` has enforced minimums — a decisions/ ADR
> directory and a CHARTER.md canonical page — then bring this repo to conformance and refresh
> the installed plugin so the standards skills actually reach the machine.

## Problem

The repo meta-structure standard audits everything around `docs/` but nothing inside it. The
checklist's only docs row is ROOT-08, `path-exists: docs/`
(`primitives-core/skills/repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md:77`) — an empty `docs/`
directory passes. There is no DOCS row family, no ADR-directory requirement, and no
canonical-page requirement, even though:

- The standard itself leans on decisions it can't point at: checklist rows cite "the
  skills-over-commands decision" (CLAUDE-07) and "the hooks-as-script-plus-config decision"
  (HOOK-01 note), but this repo has no `docs/decisions/` to hold them —
  `docs/` today is `CHARTER.md`, `images/`, `sops/` only. This repo would gap against the
  very rows it should define.
- The best worked example, `hsb3/ra-platform`, carries the shape the standard should name:
  `docs/README.md` (orientation + docs-vs-`_meta/` boundary), `docs/decisions/` with
  `README.md` (append-only convention + index) and `0000-template.md` plus 29 sequential
  ADRs. It is a reference point, not necessarily the ultimate standard — the required set is
  an open decision below.
- Conversely ra-platform has no `docs/CHARTER.md` while this repo does (with the precedence
  line "if anything anywhere disagrees with this page, this page wins",
  `docs/CHARTER.md:9`) — neither exemplar passes the union today, which is exactly why the
  minimum needs to be written down as rows, not inferred from examples.

Separately, the standard's enforcement skills never reached the installed plugin: the roster
assigns `repo-meta-structure`, `repo-compliance-audit`, `mise-en-place-scaffold`, and
`memory-taxonomy` to `plugins: [project-workflow]` (`primitives-core.yaml`) and the built
target carries them (`targets/claude-code/plugins/project-workflow/skills/`), but
`plugins.yaml` still says `version: "0.1.0"` — the same version as the installed cache
(`~/.claude/plugins/cache/dotfiles-agents/project-workflow/0.1.0/`), which predates the
standards work and contains only 9 skills. Without a version bump the plugin manager sees no
update, so the audit/scaffold skills are invisible on the machines that need them.

## Deliverables

- **A — DOCS-xx checklist rows + layout guidance.** New `## docs/ minimum planning docs`
  section in `repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md` (rows DOCS-01..05: `docs/README.md`,
  `docs/CHARTER.md`, `docs/decisions/`, `docs/decisions/README.md`,
  `docs/decisions/0000-template.md` — all `path-exists`, so zero audit-script change), plus a
  `docs/` section in `references/layout.md` stating the minimums and marking deeper taxonomy
  (design workspaces, operations, api) as per-repo variance, not rows.
- **B — Scaffold assets + mapping.** `repo-meta-structure/assets/docs/README.md` and
  `assets/docs/decisions/{README.md,0000-template.md}` (modeled on ra-platform); a `docs/`
  branch in `mise-en-place-scaffold/scripts/scaffold.py::template_source`; `docs/CHARTER.md`
  added to `AUTHORED_FILES` (flagged manual, never scaffolded — it is the canonical page).
- **C — Tests.** Extend `tests/test_audit.py` + `tests/test_scaffold.py` to cover the new
  rows, assets, and the CHARTER authored-file behavior.
- **D — Apply to this repo.** Run the scaffold, author the `docs/README.md` index, seed
  `docs/decisions/` with the template + README and backfill the already-load-bearing
  decisions the standard cites (skills-over-commands; hooks-as-script-plus-config;
  externals-tracked-not-vendored). Re-audit to 0 GAP.
- **E — Plugin refresh.** Bump `project-workflow` in `plugins.yaml`, `make build`, update the
  installed plugin so the four standards skills (and the new DOCS content) reach the machine.
  Coordinate with #27 (v2 rename/bump) — if #27 lands in the same window, E folds into it.

## Acceptance criteria

- `python3 <plugin>/skills/repo-compliance-audit/scripts/audit.py` on this repo reports the
  five DOCS rows and exits 0 GAP (or every remaining gap named + justified in the commit).
- The same audit run on a bare fixture repo reports DOCS-01..05 as GAP (rows actually fire).
- `mise-en-place-scaffold --plan` on a repo missing `docs/` plans the templated files and
  reports `docs/CHARTER.md` as manual/authored; `--apply` is additive-only (no overwrites).
- `docs/decisions/` in this repo contains `README.md`, `0000-template.md`, and at least the

- `make ci` green (existing 158 tests + new ones); `make build-check` clean after regeneration.
- The installed `project-workflow` plugin cache version is greater than 0.1.0 and contains

## Dependencies & gates

- **Fires:** `make ci` (always); targets drift guard `make build-check` (edits under

- **Does not fire:** roster drift guard `make check` (no primitive added/removed/renamed —

- **Ordering:** #27 renames all project-workflow primitives under `pw-`; whichever of the two

Applying the DOCS rows to `dotfiles-agents-workbench` and other repos (follow-up pass, same
mechanism); a full ADR backfill of this repo's history beyond the three load-bearing

## Problem

The PLANS frontmatter audit and the staged-body sync tool contradict each other, so a staged `issue-body.md` cannot satisfy both:

- `repo-compliance-audit/scripts/audit.py:318-327` scopes PLANS-01..06 over every `*.md` under `_meta/plans/` (recursive), excluding only `README.md` and `_`-prefixed path components — so a staged `<slug>/issue-body.md` is REQUIRED to carry frontmatter.
- `_meta/plans/_utils/sync-bodies.py:67` diffs the staged file RAW against the live GitHub issue body (no frontmatter stripping) — so any frontmatter on a staged body reads as permanent phantom drift.

Live consequence: the (now archived) staged body for #41 carried no frontmatter and would have gapped on PLANS-01..06 at the next audit, despite being exactly the publishable body.

**Owner ruling (2026-07-02): issue bodies are exempt from the frontmatter requirements.** A staged `issue-body.md` carries the raw publishable body; the exemption is implemented on the audit side and `sync-bodies.py` stays raw.

## Deliverables

- A — `audit.py`: add `issue-body.md` to the PLANS scope exclusions (the filename filter at `repo-compliance-audit/scripts/audit.py:327`).
- B — Standard prose: state the exemption in the PLANS scope paragraph of `repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md` and in `repo-meta-structure/references/planning-docs.md` (frontmatter-schema scope).

> **Origin:** the #24 loadability smoke's first run. The opencode agent transform passed CC frontmatter through verbatim and opencode 1.17 rejected it at load — the interim fix (PR for #24) DROPS the `tools:` key, which loses permission narrowing. Owner-ruled 2026-07-02: drop for now, redesign the baseline as the real fix.

## Problem

`primitives-core/` uses **Claude Code's formats as the base format**, and `translate.py` transforms CC → each target. That works for prose (skills) but breaks down wherever vendors have *semantically different* config surfaces:

- **`tools:`** — CC uses an allowlist (`tools: Read, Grep`); opencode uses a per-tool boolean map that toggles against defaults, so a converted list loads but does not narrow. Currently dropped in the opencode transform (agents get default toolset — widening documented in the transform docstring).
- **env interpolation** — our mcp fragments carry `"${VAR}"` (CC style); opencode does NOT substitute `${VAR}` (its form is `{env:VAR}`), so generated opencode `environment` values are passed literally. Latent bug, same family.
- **frontmatter dialects** — CC parses agent frontmatter leniently; opencode strictly (two source agents with raw multiline descriptions loaded in CC but were silently dropped by opencode until normalized).

## Direction (owner-ruled)

Develop an **agnostic base format** for primitives plus an explicit **cross-vendor mapping layer** (tool ids, permission semantics, env interpolation, frontmatter dialect), instead of CC-as-baseline.

**Research first:** someone has likely already solved cross-CLI agent/config portability in an open-source tool — survey the space (agent format converters, multi-tool dotfile managers for coding agents, e.g. the ecosystems around AGENTS.md, opencode plugins, aider/goose/codex config layers) before inventing a schema.

## Deliverables

- A — survey of prior art for cross-vendor agent/tool/config mapping; recommendation memo (adopt / adapt / build).
- B — proposed base-format spec for the primitive types we translate (agents first; skills are already near-portable), with the vendor mapping tables (tool ids, permission semantics, env interpolation).
- C — migration plan for `primitives-core/` + `translate.py` (per-type, incremental; drift guards keep working throughout).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] The `tools:` narrowing intent survives translation to opencode (or the spec explicitly records it as unsupported per vendor, surfaced in the build report — no silent widening).
- [ ] mcp env interpolation renders in each vendor's own syntax.
- [ ] `make smoke` green across the board after migration.

## Dependencies & gates

- Depends on: #24 (the smoke that detects these regressions) — merged first.
- `make ci` aggregate: fires on any translate.py/roster change.

## Out of scope

- Runtime shims or wrappers — this stays a static translation service.

## What happened

Real-world use in `mhi-raptorxai/raptorxai-infra` (2026-07-03): a fresh desk was scaffolded and three `issue-body.md` files were staged per the skill's own issue mode (bodies first, `plan.md` later). The governance toolkit could not see them:

- `reconcile.py` header reported `(3 active rows, 0 archived, 0 folders)` and emitted `DRIFT [row-no-folder] ... ACTIVE row has no plan folder on disk` — while the folders existed on disk with staged `issue-body.md` files.
- `sync-bodies.py` reported `Sync _meta/plans/*/issue-body.md vs GitHub (0 folders)` and compared nothing, even after the bodies were published as live issues #1-#3. Its stated purpose ("each folder's issue-body.md vs the live GitHub body") silently doesn't apply to any folder lacking `plan.md`.

Root cause: `disk_folders()` in `reconcile.py` (and the equivalent in `sync-bodies.py`) defines a plan folder as `(p / "plan.md").is_file()`.

## Why it matters

The skill's own workflow produces issue-body-only folders as a normal intermediate state (issue mode explicitly ships `issue-body.md` as the contract, with `plan.md` authored later "if the work needs build detail"). In that state the toolkit is blind: reconcile emits a misleading drift kind (`row-no-folder` for a folder that exists), and sync-bodies gives false assurance (0 differ) while staged bodies could drift from live issues unchecked.

Workaround used: kept such folders out of the ACTIVE table and invented a "PUBLISHED, plan pending" list in the README prose — which also reveals the README schema has no documented home for the staged-not-filed and published-no-plan lifecycle states.

## Suggested direction

- Count a folder with either artifact; distinguish `plan.md missing` (warn) from `folder missing` (drift).
- Make `sync-bodies.py` key on `issue-body.md` presence (that's the artifact it diffs).
- Give the plans-README template a documented state for pre-plan rows (or bless the prose-list pattern).

Observed with planning-desk from plugin cache 0.1.0 while repo-compliance-audit ran from 0.2.1 (mixed-version cache — separate note in the other issues). If 0.2.1+ already fixes this, close.

## Acceptance criteria

- `reconcile.py` `disk_folders()` counts a folder that has EITHER `plan.md` OR `issue-body.md`; a folder with only `issue-body.md` plus a matching ACTIVE README row no longer emits `row-no-folder` drift (add a fixture folder with only `issue-body.md`, assert reconcile exits clean).
- `sync-bodies.py` classifies and diffs folders keyed on `issue-body.md` presence: a staged `issue-body.md` differing from its live GitHub issue is reported (today 0 folders are compared when no `plan.md` exists).
- reconcile output distinguishes `plan.md missing` (warn) from `folder missing` (drift).
- `plans-README.md` documents a state for pre-plan (issue-body-only) rows, or blesses the prose-list pattern; a fresh desk with only staged bodies reconciles clean.

## Dependencies & gates

- **Blocks on:** nothing. Self-contained fix under `primitives-core/skills/planning-desk/scripts/_utils/`.
- **Gates:** `make ci` green + `targets/` regenerated via `make build` (planning-desk scripts are distributed primitives; never hand-edit `targets/`). `project-workflow` plugin version bump. No roster schema change.

> Verified against plugin source 0.2.4 (filed against 0.1.0): defect confirmed still present at `reconcile.py:122-125` and `sync-bodies.py:32`.

## What happened

`mhi-raptorxai/raptorxai-infra`, 2026-07-03: planning-desk setup mode seeded issue templates from its assets — `feature.md`, `bug.md`, `epic.md` (markdown templates). Immediately afterwards, repo-compliance-audit flagged:

```
GH-01 | GAP | missing file: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/config.yml
GH-02 | GAP | missing file: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/bug.yml
GH-03 | GAP | missing file: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/feature.yml
GH-04 | GAP | missing file: .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/epic.yml
```

So a repo that adopts the plugin's own planning-desk defaults audits as non-conformant against the plugin's own repo-meta-structure standard: one skill ships `.md` issue forms, the sibling standard's checklist requires the `.yml` issue-forms set plus `config.yml`.

Also, planning-desk's conformance gate (`conformance.py`) reads required sections from `.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/*.md` — if a repo carries the standard's `.yml` forms instead, it's unclear the desk's conformance checking still works, so the two skills may be unsatisfiable simultaneously rather than just inconsistent.

## Suggested direction

Pick one template format for the plugin (issue-forms `.yml` seems to be where the standard is) and make planning-desk seed it and parse it; or teach the checklist to accept either format. Either way, the audit -> scaffold -> desk loop shouldn't fight itself.

Version caveat: planning-desk executed from plugin cache 0.1.0, repo-compliance-audit from 0.2.1. If planning-desk 0.2.x already seeds yml forms, the remaining bug is just the stale-cache/mixed-version behavior (see also: the marketplace cache served two different plugin versions for sibling skills in one session).

---

## Corrected scope (verified against plugin source 0.2.4)

This issue was filed against cache 0.1.0. Re-verifying against current source narrows it: **one half is live, one half is invalid.**

- **LIVE — the template-format conflict is real.** `primitives-core/skills/planning-desk/assets/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/` ships `bug.md` / `feature.md` / `epic.md` (markdown templates, no `config.yml`), while `repo-meta-structure/references/checklist.md:53-56` GH-01..04 require `config.yml` + `bug.yml` + `feature.yml` + `epic.yml`. `SKILL.md:104-106` and `_config.template.md:18-20` still seed/point at the `.md` set, so a repo adopting planning-desk defaults fails the sibling audit GH-01..04.

- planning-desk seeds the `.yml` issue-forms set (`config.yml` + `bug.yml` + `feature.yml` + `epic.yml`) that GH-01..04 expect, OR the checklist is taught to accept either format; a fresh `planning-desk` setup then passes `repo-compliance-audit` GH-01..04.
- `SKILL.md` setup section and `_config.template.md` no longer point only at `.md` template paths.
- `conformance.py` is left unchanged (confirmed already format-agnostic).

**Owner decision:** which format wins — ship `.yml` forms in planning-desk (align to the standard) [recommended default], or teach the checklist to also accept `.md`?

- **Gates:** `make ci` green + `targets/` regenerated via `make build` when planning-desk assets change; `project-workflow` version bump. Relates to `repo-meta-structure` GH-01..04.

content.body:
Found 2026-07-04 while running the board overhaul on a real org project (mhi-raptorxai project #5), project-workflow plugin 0.2.1.

## Bug
`skills/github-project-board/scripts/*.py` share a `graphql()` helper that passes every variable with `gh api graphql -f k=v`. `-f` is always a **string** field, but the queries declare typed variables (`$n:Int!` in `PROJECT_ID_Q`, etc.), so current `gh` fails with:

```
gh: Variable $n of type Int! was provided invalid value
```

This breaks `board-export.py`, `board-apply.py`, and `board-fields.py` on first contact — the whole export→analyze→apply loop is dead until patched.

## Fix
One character in the shared helper — use `-F` (typed: coerces numbers/booleans, leaves strings alone) for variables; keep `-f` for the query text itself:

```python
def graphql(query: str, **fvars: str) -> dict:
    args = ["api", "graphql", "-f", "query=" + query]
    for k, v in fvars.items():
        args += ["-F", f"{k}={v}"]   # was -f
```

Verified: with this patch all three scripts ran clean against the org project (92-item export, 384-row changeset applied, idempotent re-run 0 changed).

## Two adjacent paper cuts from the same session (fold in or split, your call)
1. **Changeset header row:** `board-apply.py` requires the `issue<TAB>field<TAB>value` header (documented in the docstring) and silently plans `0 changed · 0 unchanged · 0 skipped` on a headerless file — a headerless TSV looks like a successful no-op. Consider exiting non-zero when zero rows parse, and/or telling the board-analyst agent prompt to always emit the header (the bundled analyst produced headerless TSVs).
2. **`--owner-type` default is `user`:** on an org project the failure surfaces as the (misleading) Int! error above rather than "project not found". content.body:
## What happened

Standing up a board for `mhi-raptorxai/raptorxai-infra` (org project, 2026-07-03), all three board scripts in `github-project-board/scripts/` failed on first contact:

1. **`Int!` variable passed as string.** The shared `graphql()` helper passes every variable with `gh api graphql -f`, but `PROJECT_ID_Q` declares `$n:Int!`. `-f` sends the value as a JSON string, so every invocation dies with `Variable $n of type Int! was provided invalid value`. The scripts cannot work against any project as shipped. Fix: use `-F` for the int variable (careful: only for the typed-int variable — blanket `-F`-for-digit-values breaks `String!` args like all-numeric single-select option ids, which really occur; Impact option ids on our board were all-digits).

2. **Changeset header row is required but undocumented.** `board-apply.py` parses the TSV with `csv.DictReader`, so a file matching the documented contract ("TSV diff, one row per cell: `issue<TAB>field<TAB>value`") parses to zero rows and reports `0 changed · 0 unchanged` — success-shaped output for a total no-op. Fix: document the `issue\tfield\tvalue` header in §9, and/or make the parser tolerate headerless files, and/or exit non-zero when 0 rows parse.

3. Minor: §9's example invocations omit `--owner-type org`; the default is `user` and the error when wrong ("project not found" only after the Int fix) doesn't hint at it.

## Repro

`python3 scripts/board-export.py -o <any> -n <any>` → the Int! error, before auth or owner-type even matter.

Observed on plugin cache 0.2.1. Patched locally (copy in job tmp) with `-F` only for `n` + a header row; the full loop then worked end to end (export → 73-row changeset → apply → idempotent re-run).

> **Tracking:** from the strategy desk — G2 product brief ratified by Henry 2026-07-13 (desk: `deliverables/foreman-product-brief.md`, "spot on"). Filed per the 2026-07-11 standing rule: new development is **spec-first through the workbench**, promote through the gate. First **bundle** (plugin) intake under the ADR 0012 governance charter v2; applies the ADR 0013 tier doctrine.

## Problem

Delegated multi-agent work today depends on `fable-foreman` (model-specific) plus ad-hoc judgment about how much context each agent gets. Henry's fable-optimization experiments found the cost/quality optimum at **~100k context per agent, cycled through handoff + clear + resume** — but nothing enforces or even encourages that rhythm, and nothing packages the tier discipline (smart models decide, cheap models execute).

`foreman` turns the lived delegation workflow into a product: any orchestrating session can run the tier model with pre-built agent profiles, standard handoffs, and hooks that nudge the context cycle — so delegation quality stops depending on remembering the doctrine.

**Buy-before-build (G3):** the 2026-07-13 tooling census found `fable-optimization` already runs local `context-watermark` and `handoff-freshness` hooks in `settings.local.json`. The build starts by **promoting and hardening those**, not writing new ones.

## Bundle contents (workflow: tiered delegation + context cycling)

| Component | Content |
| --- | --- |
| **foreman skill** | `fable-foreman` generalized: model-agnostic orchestration — definition of done, delegation architecture selection, evaluation gates (tier-1 behavior per ADR 0013) |
| **Base agent profiles** | Tier templates: {build, explore, review} × model tier. Profiles reference **tiers, not hard model IDs** — a small mapping table pins tier → current model ID in one place |
| **handoff skill** | Shared membership (ADR 0012 REQ-4): single canonical copy, bundled here *and* wherever else handoffs matter |
| **Hooks** | Context-watermark nudge (approaching ~100k → prompt handoff + compact) and handoff-freshness check (warn on commit/PR when `HANDOFF.md` is stale — the ADR 0013 lead-agent convention) |

## Deliverables

- **A — Scope doc first** (spec-driven intake): lands the ratified G2 brief's requirements in the candidate folder — component inventory, the fable-optimization hooks as the promotion source, known overlaps (J4), acceptance mapped to the H/J gate. No code before A exists.
- **B — `incubator/foreman/`** bundle: skill + agent profiles + hooks + bundled handoff skill, incubator layout, hook-dir format (config.json + script).
- **C — `REGISTRY.md` rows** (`incubating`, `origin: refactor of fable-foreman / promotion of fable-optimization hooks`) with gate status.

## Requirements (from the ratified brief; REQ → acceptance criteria)

1. **Model-agnostic foreman skill.** *AC:* no model-specific instructions outside the tier→model mapping table; invoking on an Opus- or Fable-led session produces the same procedure.
2. **Tier profiles invocable as agents.** *AC:* each profile is a valid agent definition that loads in Claude Code; each states its tier, job scope (build/explore/review), and the context it must NOT be given; tier-3 profiles fit the "one job, minimal context, optional handoff file" contract.
3. **Tier→model mapping single-sourced.** *AC:* changing the current model for a tier is a one-file edit; profiles pick it up without individual edits.
4. **Context-cycle hooks.** *AC:* watermark hook fires a visible nudge before the ~100k boundary in a real session; handoff-freshness hook warns when `HANDOFF.md` predates the work being committed; both hook-dir format, stdlib-only per the gate's H-checks.
5. **Branch-handoff convention encoded.** *AC:* the bundled handoff skill implements ADR 0013's model — `HANDOFF.md` lead-agent-only pre-commit/PR; `handoff-{branch}-{agent}-{datetime}.md` for any agent.
6. **README** per readme-value-and-proof (ADR 0012 REQ-2). *AC:* README states the value prop and shows the workflow, not a component inventory. Feedback mechanism stated: issues on `hsb3/dotfiles-agents` labeled `plugin:foreman`, triaged in the maintenance window (G5).

## Out of scope

opencode translation of the hooks (deferred per CANON/ADR 0007 — hooks are CC-only today); any new tier-2/tier-1 automation beyond the profiles; changes to the workbench gate.

## Acceptance criteria (issue-level)

- [ ] Scope doc exists in the candidate folder and predates the implementation commit.
- [ ] All six REQ ACs above met.
- [ ] Hard checks pass (`make promote-check` per item); J1–J4 tracked on the registry rows (promotion itself is a separate, later step — J1 needs ≥2 real uses).

## Dependencies & gates

- Governed by ADR 0012 (charter v2, G-gates), ADR 0013 (tier doctrine, handoff convention), ADR 0014 (lands in the dev/main distribution model at promotion).
- Sources: `fable-foreman` skill (refactor origin) and `fable-optimization` local hooks (promotion origin).
- Workbench CI + promotion gate (H1–H6, J1–J4) at exit, per `docs/promotion-gate.md`.

content.body:
**Epic — system cohesion + value evaluation (pre-1.0).** Extensive testing and evaluation confirming that `deskkit` + the two plugins + the librarian + the PM system form a **cohesive system that behaves as expected** AND provides **significant value over (a) a naive approach and (b) an off-the-shelf alternative**. (Owner-added pre-1.0 requirement, 2026-07-19.)

**Deliverables**
- An **end-to-end system-behavior test suite** exercising the whole system on a real desk (cold start → profile → librarian sweep/patrol/fix → PM graph create/transition/gate/cascade → plugin skills/agents/hooks → release), not just per-module unit tests.
- A **cohesion assessment**: the modules + surfaces (binary, MCP, CLI, TUI, plugins) behave as one system, with the seams (DocumentValidator, tool-core, store) proven under real workflows.
- A **value evaluation** with a defined rubric + baselines: measure the system against (1) a naive approach (hand-maintained markdown/handoff + manual hygiene) and (2) a relevant off-the-shelf alternative — on the tasks the product claims to improve (session continuity, gate-enforced work state, safe automated hygiene). Report where it clearly wins, ties, or loses.

**Acceptance**
- The E2E suite passes on a clean environment and is wired into CI (or a documented release gate).
- A written evaluation with the rubric, the baselines, the measurements, and an **honest verdict** on "cohesive + significantly better than naive/off-the-shelf." If it does NOT clearly beat the alternatives on a claimed dimension, that is a finding that feeds back into scope before 1.0.

**Open scoping (short design step at lane start):** the exact baselines, the off-the-shelf comparator(s), and the value rubric.

_Provenance: owner directive 2026-07-19 (decision 0021 fork F7 / roadmap Lane 8)._

## Deliverables
1. A PB-served page (custom Go route under `serve`) providing the same multi-turn stewardship session the `chat` REPL exposes — over the same `internal/agent` session type, same gated tool registry.
2. Write boundary identical to the TUI: no new write path, `apply_fix` env-gated, `restore` unreachable from the surface.
3. Setup docs as actual behavior (extend the README's interactive-session section).

## Criteria
- Reachable from a running `serve` in one browser visit (documented URL), no separate frontend build toolchain required at runtime.
- Session history bounded (the REPL caps at 40 messages — same or better).
- Neutrality lint green; all existing gates green.

content.body:
## Context

First real-world brownfield adoption of the standard: `product-exec-desk`, plugin + deskkit v0.7.0, baseline patrol run `patrol-20260719T161433Z` (fresh store, 144 files).

## Problem

All 3 R5 findings from the baseline were false positives. R5 fired on:

- `analyses/2026-07-18-portfolio-inventory.md` (152 lines, "references filed issue #7")
- `analyses/horizon-1-work-packages.md` (132 lines, "references filed issue #5")
- `analyses/product-roadmap.md` (113 lines, "references filed issue #631")

None of these is a graduated doc. They **cite** issues as evidence or pointers:

- the inventory mentions org board `#7` precisely to say "work-state truth lives there, never snapshot counts" (i.e. it's *following* K2, and it's a dated point-in-time artifact — the adherence checklist's own procedure says dated frozen snapshots are not re-checked);
- the work-packages plan cites `#595/#187/#188/#631` as verification citations in its live-state-check section;
- the roadmap cites `#631` once as a convergence gate.

The decomposition/roadmap content exists nowhere but the desk. Applying the suggested collapse would have destroyed the only copy. The heuristic (issue reference + line count) cannot distinguish "this doc graduated into that issue" from "this doc cites that issue as evidence".

## Suggestion

- Require an explicit graduation marker before R5 fires — e.g. a frontmatter field (`graduated_to: <issue-url>`) or a ruled "Graduated to" section — rather than inferring graduation from any `#N` reference.
- Exempt dated point-in-time artifacts (`YYYY-MM-DD-*`) from R5, matching the checklist's frozen-snapshot exclusion.
- Until then, consider labeling R5 advisory in patrol output so adopters don't treat it as a conformance failure.

Triage record on the adopting desk: `product-exec-desk/_meta/adoption-plan.md` § Execution record.

content.body:
## Context

First real-world adoption (`product-exec-desk`, v0.7.0). The desk-pm plugin's `.mcp.json` is:

```json
{ "desk-pm": { "command": "deskkit", "args": ["mcp-serve"], "env": { "PM_ENABLED": "true" } } }
```

## Problem

On a machine where deskkit is not yet installed — which is exactly the first-adoption state, since installing deskkit is a *step of* the adoption the plugin drives — the MCP server fails to mount at session start with no surfaced error. Two knock-on effects observed:

1. The session that performs the adoption has no `mcp__desk-pm__*` tools, and (because MCP servers attach at session start) installing deskkit mid-session doesn't help.
2. The `desk-pm:pm-operator` subagent, whose tool list is the twelve PM MCP tools, spawns with essentially no tools at all (only `Read` in our case). It handled this correctly per its boundaries (stopped and reported), but the failure is only discoverable after dispatching it.

Workaround used: drove `deskkit mcp-serve` directly over stdio JSON-RPC (initialize → tools/list → tools/call) from a script; store population worked fine that way, and the plugin tools mount normally in the next session.

## Suggestion

- A preflight/health signal: if `deskkit` is absent from PATH, surface an actionable message (install pointer + "restart session after install") instead of a silent mount failure.
- A note in the brownfield-adoption skill's prerequisites: deskkit must be installed **and the session restarted** before the desk-pm tool surface exists — mid-session installs need the stdio fallback or a new session.
content.title: desk-pm MCP server silently absent when deskkit not on PATH at session start; pm-operator spawns toolless

content.body:
## Context

First real-world adoption (`product-exec-desk`, v0.7.0), adherence sweep during the K24 conformance pass.

## Problem

The conventions-standard exemption classes cover "template files (the standard-free scaffold)", but not the **instantiated copies** of scaffold-shipped instruments. Concretely: `_meta/improvement-log.md` is shipped by the scaffold without frontmatter and rendered into the desk; a frontmatter checker then flags the instantiated file (K3: no frontmatter), and there is no ruled basis to dismiss the finding — we had to special-case it by hand after diffing against the shipped template.

The same gray zone applies to desk working notes that follow a template shape (checklists, skim lists): the exemption list is closed, so anything not on it needs frontmatter, but the scaffold itself produces files that violate that.

## Suggestion

Rule it one way or the other:

- either extend the exemption class to "scaffold-shipped instruments, as instantiated" (`improvement-log.md` by basename, like the directory-index `README.md` rule), or
- ship the scaffold instruments with conformant frontmatter so instantiated desks are clean by construction (probably the better end state — one less exemption).

Ledger entry on the adopting desk: `product-exec-desk/_meta/improvement-log.md` INS-02.

content.body: Pre-existing, surfaced during D4 verification (PR #66): `deskkit <unknown>` — including `deskkit pm …` on a PM-disabled desk — prints `Error: unknown command …` but exits 0, because PocketBase's `Execute()` discards cobra's parse error and the RunE wrapper can only cover registered commands. Scripts can't detect the failure. Base-identical behavior (not introduced by D4), but the feature-gated `pm` group makes this path likelier. Fix candidates: cobra `SilenceErrors` + explicit error propagation around PB Execute, or a custom unknown-command handler. Found by adversarial verification of #66; epic #55 follow-up.

content.body:
While answering a question about kit integration, found a factual overstatement in [ADR 0006](docs/decisions/0006-kit-port-schema-reconciliation.md).

**Claim (Decision §1, ~line 36):** kits are *"consumed by both lanes (plugin skills today; the PM module's document gates next)."*
Also echoed in Alternatives (~line 103): *"Kits are consumed by the librarian/PM module too, not just the plugin."*

**Reality (as of v0.6.0):** no plugin skill references `kits/` at all — `rg -i '\bkit' plugin/claude-plugin/skills` returns zero hits. The only runtime-adjacent code touching `kits/` is `librarian/templates/kit_render_test.go`, a render-**compatibility** guard (reads `kits/analysis/template.md`, renders it through the fixer's `Render()`), not an integration. The actual "today" consumers are the contract/guard layer only: `scripts/check-kits.mjs`, `scripts/check-neutrality.mjs` (scan surface), and `schema/doctypes.yaml`. The librarian binary can't even reach `kits/` (`go:embed` can't cross `..`; kits sit at repo root by design). Real consumption is deferred — #36 (librarian template-selection, needs a design ruling) and #55 D2/D3 (PM module document gates).

**Ask:** once the core/modules + kit-consumption work settles (checkouts actively in flight now, so not editing the ADR yet), correct the ADR per the erratum discipline in \`rules/project-protocol.md\` §1 — a dated \`> **Correction (YYYY-MM-DD):**\` callout striking the "plugin skills today" phrasing, since a falsified premise shouldn't read as current truth. Low severity; documentation-accuracy only.
content.title: ADR 0006: 'plugin skills today' overstates kit consumption — no skill references kits/
